name: Burrows–Wheeler sentinel transform
definition: Let S=x⊕$ with unique least sentinel $, N=|S|, and π(j) the starting index of the j-th lexicographically sorted cyclic rotation. Set B[j]=S[(π(j)−1) mod N]. Define C(c)=#{i:B[i]<c}, Occ(c,j)=#{i<j:B[i]=c}, and LF(j)=C(B[j])+Occ(B[j],j). Starting at the unique r with B[r]=$, fill S[N−1−k]=B[r] and update r←LF(r) for k=0,…,N−1; then remove the terminal sentinel.
variables: x finite input sequence, $ reserved least symbol, S augmented sequence, N augmented length, π rotation order, B transformed column, C cumulative smaller-symbol count, Occ exclusive occurrence rank, LF last-to-first permutation, r current row
assumptions: Finite totally ordered alphabet, sentinel absent from x and smaller than all input symbols, exact symbol comparisons, zero-based indexing, known block length and alphabet order; empty x is represented by the sentinel alone
limitations: Explicit rotation materialization uses O(N²) storage and O(N² log N) worst-case symbol comparisons; a suffix array of the sentinel-terminated sequence can supply the same order without materializing rotations. Inversion uses O(N+K) time and storage with preordered dense alphabet of size K and direct-index counts; arbitrary symbol sorting adds cost. Transformation preserves the symbol multiset plus sentinel and is not itself compression
failure_conditions: Sentinel absent, duplicated or part of the original input alphabet
Invalid symbol ordering or transformed column whose LF orbit from the sentinel does not visit every row exactly once and return to its start
computation: Sort rotations or compute the sentinel-terminated suffix array, emit predecessor symbols; count symbols and exclusive occurrences to build LF. Reject invalid alphabet or sentinel and reject a premature cycle or failure to close after N steps before returning reconstructed input.

source.citation: Burrows and Wheeler (1994), A Block-sorting Lossless Data Compression Algorithm, SRC Research Report 124, section 2, pp. 2–4 (rotation and occurrence-ranked inverse). https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/2223/Bioinfo/papers/burrows_wheeler.pdf ; sentinel-only framing and single-cycle validity check independently derived from unique sentinel rotation order.

application: General reversible sequence rearrangement; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite sequence of exact comparable symbols and reserved least sentinel, or a framed transformed column for inversion.
incompatible_methods: Assuming the transform alone reduces bit length
Accepting a malformed last column with multiple LF cycles
mechanism_note: Right-rotation of rows ending in the same symbol preserves their relative lexicographic order, giving LF by stable occurrence rank. A unique sentinel distinguishes every rotation and identifies the original row, so LF traverses one cycle of length N. Unlike suffix-array construction, the output is a reversible symbol permutation rather than an index; suffix ordering is a reusable subroutine, not an equivalent transform.

name: Move-to-front rank transform
definition: With shared initial permutation A of K distinct symbols, at input position t set r_t=index_A(x_t) and A←[x_t] concatenated with A after deleting x_t. For decoding set x_t=A[r_t] before applying the same update, requiring 0≤r_t<K.
variables: A mutable ordered alphabet, K alphabet size, x_t input or recovered symbol at position t, r_t zero-based rank
assumptions: Finite nonempty shared alphabet with identical initial order, exact symbol equality, no insertion of new symbols, externally framed rank sequence; empty input produces empty output
limitations: Simple list representation uses O(nK) worst-case time and O(K) working storage for n symbols; integer ranks require separate coding to yield a bitstream. Locality may produce small ranks, but there is no finite-input compression guarantee and rank corruption can desynchronize subsequent state
failure_conditions: Unknown input symbol or duplicated initial alphabet symbol
Noninteger or out-of-range decoded rank, mismatched initial order or missing framing
computation: For each input symbol find its current position, emit that rank and move it to the front; in decoding validate the rank before retrieving and moving its symbol. Encoder and decoder maintain identical list state inductively.

source.citation: Bentley, Sleator, Tarjan and Wei (1986), A Locally Adaptive Data Compression Scheme, Communications of the ACM 29(4), 320–330, p. 321, sections 2–3. DOI 10.1145/5684.5688. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~sleator/papers/adaptive-data-compression.pdf ; fixed shared alphabet and zero-based ranks are an explicit restricted convention, not the full new-word or integer coding scheme.

application: General reversible recency-rank transformation for finite symbol sequences; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite symbol sequence with known ordered alphabet, or a framed sequence of integer ranks and the same ordered alphabet.
incompatible_methods: Treating rank stream as a complete compressed bitstream
Changing the initial alphabet independently at decoder
mechanism_note: The state is an ordering of fixed symbols by recency, rather than an expanding phrase dictionary or a global rotation permutation. Rank emission plus deterministic list update is invertible with shared state, and can be composed with the Burrows–Wheeler transform without being equivalent to it.
